prompts.title: Recent Form Rhythm
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 6–10 seconds, adapted to the spoken words. Editorial variant: a kinetic typography block built from Spanish team labels, Club Brugge KV and Racing Club de Lens, plus generic sports headings such as ‘Forma’, ‘Ritmo’ and ‘Últimos partidos’. No statistical axes, no counts and no sample claims appear here. Composition: charcoal #101412 field with a warm white #edf0e6 typographic spine; Brugge words rise in lime #c5ed74, Lens words slide in slate #8ca6bf. Rhythmic emphasis: each team name lands on a beat, then offsets into a diagonal duet; thin warm-white rules pulse like a sports bumper. Keep one focal point at the upper-middle; reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles. Camera: slow vertical push with a tiny lateral drift. Transition: a typographic match cut where the last rule becomes the chart baseline. Exit: names compress into a warm-white line that wipes away. Statistical variant: grouped horizontal count bars for Victorias, Empates and Derrotas, one team group above the other, using values {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}} for Club Brugge KV and {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}} for Racing Club de Lens. Unit is partidos; common shared baseline at zero. Spanish labels appear directly on each bar and as category labels. Source/sample footer: ‘Fuente: Bzzoiro · muestra: {{home.n}} partidos’ for Club Brugge KV and ‘Fuente: Bzzoiro · muestra: {{away.n}} partidos’ for Racing Club de Lens; identify each sample explicitly rather than assuming equal samples. Entry: axis fades in, bars grow from the shared baseline with staggered timing. Main comparison: within each category, the Brugge and Lens bars sit close enough to read as a pair. Emphasis: the longest supplied bar in each sample receives a lime cap and a short label leader, without adding interpretation. Camera: almost static, with a subtle push toward the category labels. Transition: bars retract into the baseline, source line holds, then a charcoal wipe reveals the next scene. Exit: the sample annotations remain legible for the final beat, then fade with the subtitle-safe lower quarter untouched.

prompts.title: Goals For and Against on the Pitch
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 6–10 seconds, timed to the spoken words. Editorial variant: an illustrative football pitch viewed top-down, with Brugge and Lens rendered as abstract team shapes rather than kits. Spanish team labels sit at opposite ends; generic headings such as ‘Ataque’ and ‘Defensa’ are the only text. A single warm-white ball path traces from midfield toward the edge of the final third, then loops back, never ending at the goal, so it cannot read as an invented match event or scoreline. Composition: charcoal #101412 pitch, warm white #edf0e6 lines, lime #c5ed74 energy for Club Brugge KV, slate #8ca6bf energy for Racing Club de Lens. One focal point follows the ball. Camera: slow overhead drift with a gentle parallax on the pitch lines. Transition: the pitch lines straighten and morph into a chart grid. Exit: the ball path collapses into a lime point that fades. Keep the lower quarter clear for permanent yellow subtitles. Statistical variant: two clustered bar groups, ‘Goles a favor’ and ‘Goles en contra’, each containing a Brugge bar and a Lens bar. Values are {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}} for Club Brugge KV, {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}} for Racing Club de Lens. Shared scale in goles, common baseline at zero, direct Spanish labels above each bar. Source/sample footer: ‘Fuente: Bzzoiro · muestra: {{home.n}} partidos’ and ‘Fuente: Bzzoiro · muestra: {{away.n}} partidos’, with source and sample attached to the chart, not detached in a corner. Entry: grid appears first, then bars grow upward from the baseline. Main comparison: within each group the two team bars are paired; a thin warm-white bracket links each pair without calculating a new value. Emphasis: the taller supplied bar in each group gets a soft lime edge glow; labels remain upright. Camera: slight vertical tilt from group label to bars. Transition: a horizontal wipe moves from the pitch illustration into the bar chart, then bars settle. Exit: source line persists, bars shrink to baseline, and the lower quarter stays reserved for subtitles.

prompts.title: Clean-Sheet Shield
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 6–10 seconds, matched to the spoken line. Editorial variant: defensive energy expressed as a stylised shield, with no axes, no sample claims and no invented saves or match events. A large abstract shield outline sits centre-frame in warm white #edf0e6 over charcoal #101412; lime #c5ed74 blocks assemble for Club Brugge KV from the left, slate #8ca6bf blocks assemble for Racing Club de Lens from the right. Spanish labels are limited to team names and generic words such as ‘Defensa’ and ‘Solidez’. Rhythmic emphasis: blocks lock into place on beats, the shield pulses once, then holds. Keep one focal point at the shield centre and reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles. Camera: slow push-in with slight rotational settle. Transition: the shield outline becomes a horizontal chart frame. Exit: blocks retract outward as the shield line fades. Statistical variant: paired horizontal bars for ‘Arcos en cero’, one bar for Club Brugge KV using {{home.clean}} and one for Racing Club de Lens using {{away.clean}}. Unit is partidos; common shared baseline; no conversion into rates. Spanish labels sit at the bar ends, with category title ‘Arcos en cero’. Source/sample footer: ‘Fuente: Bzzoiro · muestra: {{home.n}} partidos’ for Club Brugge KV and ‘Fuente: Bzzoiro · muestra: {{away.n}} partidos’ for Racing Club de Lens, keeping sample sizes attached. Entry: frame draws first, then bars extend from the shared baseline; if a supplied bar resolves to the baseline, show a small outlined marker at the zero line rather than a filled bar. Main comparison: the two bars align vertically for direct reading. Emphasis: a thin lime underline highlights the Brugge sample label, while a slate underline highlights Lens; neither adds a claim. Camera: subtle drift along the bars. Transition: the chart frame collapses back into the shield silhouette, then a charcoal wipe clears the scene. Exit: source/sample line holds for one beat and fades without entering the subtitle-safe lower quarter.

prompts.title: Grounded Tension Synthesis
prompts.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 6–10 seconds, built around the spoken narrative. Editorial variant: a two-team reveal with narrative emphasis. Club Brugge KV appears first as a lime #c5ed74 light sweep across charcoal #101412, then Racing Club de Lens answers as a slate #8ca6bf sweep; warm white #edf0e6 typography forms Spanish team labels and generic headings such as ‘Forma’, ‘Ataque’ and ‘Duelo’. No axes, no counts and no sample claims appear in this editorial block. Composition: split diagonally, Brugge upper-left, Lens lower-right, with one focal point at the collision line. Camera: slow lateral truck that reveals each team in turn. Transition: the collision line straightens into the divider between two statistical panels. Exit: both team names compress into a warm-white seam that wipes away. Reserve the lower quarter for permanent yellow subtitles. Statistical variant: two stacked mini-panels, not one combined index. Upper panel ‘Victorias’ uses count bars for Club Brugge KV {{home.wins}} and Racing Club de Lens {{away.wins}}, unit partidos, shared scale within that panel. Lower panel ‘Goles a favor’ uses bars for Club Brugge KV {{home.gf}} and Racing Club de Lens {{away.gf}}, unit goles, shared scale within that panel. Source/sample footer: ‘Fuente: Bzzoiro · muestra: {{home.n}} partidos’ and ‘Fuente: Bzzoiro · muestra: {{away.n}} partidos’, attached to both panels. Spanish labels stay direct. Entry: upper panel resolves first, lower panel follows, each from its own baseline. Main comparison: read wins as wins and goals as goals; never compare the two units against each other. Emphasis: the supplied contrast in each panel receives a lime or slate edge highlight, not a prediction. No model estimate appears because no published estimate is supplied; this is historical last-matches context only. Camera: gentle vertical tilt between panels. Transition: the panel divider becomes the wipe into the next scene. Exit: source/sample line holds, bars retract, lower quarter remains clear.
